drift_notes: [claude-loops-scheduling] Latest Claude Code version as of today is v2.1.215 (July 19, 2026). Four releases landed after the 2026-07-12 baseline: v2.1.212 (Jul 17), v2.1.214 (Jul 18), and v2.1.215 (Jul 19), plus v2.1.211 (Jul 15).

[claude-loops-scheduling] NEW GUARDRAILS (post-baseline): a session-wide WebSearch tool-call limit (default 200, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION) and a per-session subagent spawn cap (default 200, CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION, reset by /clear) were added and are described in the changelog as explicitly intended to stop runaway search and delegation loops. These are the first CLI-side runaway-loop circuit breakers directly relevant to this bucket.

[claude-loops-scheduling] NEW: MCP tool calls running longer than 2 minutes now move to the background automatically so the session stays usable; threshold configurable or disableable via CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS.

[claude-loops-scheduling] RENAME: /fork now copies the conversation into a new background session with its own row in claude agents; the in-session subagent it used to launch is now /subtask. Any repo guidance referencing /fork as an in-session subagent is stale.
[claude-loops-scheduling] DEPRECATION: the Task tool's mode parameter is deprecated and now ignored; subagents inherit the parent session's permission mode by default.

[claude-loops-scheduling] LOOP-RELEVANT FIX (v2.1.214): hooks returning exit code 2 were not blocking as documented when the hook's stdout JSON failed schema validation. Since /goal is a prompt-based Stop hook and Stop hooks are the custom termination primitive, any pre-v2.1.214 measurement of hook-based loop control may have been silently non-blocking.

[claude-loops-scheduling] LOOP-RELEVANT FIX (v2.1.214): scheduled tasks were refusing their own configured prompt as untrusted input; the fired prompt is now delivered as the session's assigned task. Pre-fix, scheduled loops could no-op on their own prompt.

[claude-loops-scheduling] LOOP-RELEVANT FIX (v2.1.210): a hook callback timeout was being misreported to the model as a user rejection, which made unattended sessions stop and wait. This is a direct silent-stall failure mode for long-running unattended loops before v2.1.210.

[claude-loops-scheduling] ROUTINES FIX (v2.1.211): routines with no schedule trigger (API- or GitHub-only) reported a next run time in the year 1; the CLI now shows none. Corroborated independently by the routines doc, which states 'Before v2.1.211'.

[claude-loops-scheduling] BEHAVIOR CHANGE (v2.1.215): Claude no longer invokes the /verify and /code-review skills on its own. Combined with the v2.1.196 rule that a scheduled fire only runs self-invocable skills, this plausibly changes what '/loop <interval> /verify' does. Flagged as derived, not confirmed.
[claude-loops-scheduling] URL DRIFT: the registered source https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-loop now 404s. Canonical location is https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop.

[claude-loops-scheduling] NEW SOURCE DISCOVERED: https://claude.com/blog/getting-started-with-loops is an official Anthropic loop-engineering guide linked directly from the tier-1 agent-loop docs. It supplies the turn-based / goal-based / time-based / proactive taxonomy mapped onto /goal, /loop, and /schedule. Recommend registering it (tier 3, 30-day recheck).

[claude-loops-scheduling] OTHER CANDIDATE SOURCES SURFACED but not yet fetched in depth: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/managed-agents (Scaling Managed Agents: decoupling the brain from the hands) and https://claude.com/blog/harnessing-claudes-intelligence (Agent Harness Design: 3 Patterns). Both are on-focus for long-running harness design and worth registering next pass.

[claude-loops-scheduling] STREAM OBSERVABILITY (v2.1.211): --forward-subagent-text and CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT now include subagent text and thinking in stream-json output, which materially improves the ability to instrument a long-running loop's inner agents.

[claude-hooks-permissions] Release floor moved: CHANGELOG top entry is v2.1.215, while the docs' inline min-version markers reach v2.1.211. Any baseline pinned at or before v2.1.211 is now behind. The changelog carries no dates, so exact attribution of which releases landed after 2026-07-12 is not possible from this source.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.211 materially loosened an auto mode default: pushing to ANY branch of the working repository, including the default branch, is now allowed without a prompt. Previously only the starting branch, Claude-created branches, and routine default-branch pushes were allowed; before v2.1.203 any direct push to the default branch was blocked. Branches whose names mark them as deploy or publication targets (production, release, gh-pages) are explicitly NOT covered and are still judged on their own terms. Guidance written against the older, stricter push default is now wrong.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.211 removed the 'Default / protected branches' context slot from autoMode.environment, which previously treated main and master as protected until you named others. Configuration examples that set that slot are now obsolete.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.211 added a new default block rule: committing or pushing a change that would send secrets or sensitive data outside the repository when it runs, or that widens what a deploy exposes. It applies on any branch, applies even when the repository is public, and fires when the change lands whether or not the landing triggers the pipeline.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.212 added `claude auto-mode reset`, which removes the autoMode section from ~/.claude/settings.json (confirmation prompt, --yes to skip). Managed-settings and --settings autoMode rules survive the reset.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.210 changed the classifier model: it now runs on Claude Sonnet 5 by default rather than following the session's /model selection, with a server-side Anthropic override taking precedence. Fallbacks apply when the session model is Sonnet 4.6, when availableModels excludes Sonnet 5, or when the session runs on Fable 5. This directly stales third-party write-ups describing the second-stage classifier as Sonnet 4.6.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.208 extended the rm -rf / and rm -rf ~ circuit breaker to fire on command substitution ($(...) and backticks) and process substitution (<(...)), whether the removal sits inside the substitution or elsewhere in the command. Before v2.1.208 those forms went to the classifier instead of prompting. Same release added `claude auto-mode defaults --label`.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.207 removed the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1 requirement on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude apps gateway sessions (it had been required from v2.1.158 through v2.1.206; the variable is still accepted but has no effect). The same release stopped the classifier reading autoMode from .claude/settings.local.json, and fixed hook `if` conditions so file-path patterns like "Edit(src/**)" match as documented.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.205 added an auto mode block rule covering writes to Claude Code's own session transcripts (the .jsonl files under ~/.claude/projects/), directly or via shell. Reading transcripts is not blocked. Rationale given is defense in depth: a tampered transcript entry reaches every later check once the session resumes.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.200 relabeled the `default` permission mode to 'Manual' across the CLI, VS Code, JetBrains and desktop, and added `manual` as an accepted alias for the value (e.g. --permission-mode manual). The config value remains `default`, which is what hooks and SDK integrations continue to use - so hook input parsing on permission_mode should still expect the string 'default', not 'manual'.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.211 added `"fork"` as a SessionStart hook source value, alongside startup/resume/clear/compact. Matcher configurations that enumerate SessionStart sources will not fire on forked sessions unless updated.

[claude-hooks-permissions] v2.1.215 stopped Claude auto-invoking the /verify and /code-review skills; they must now be invoked explicitly. Relevant to any workflow that assumed those ran on their own.

[claude-hooks-permissions] Tier-5 practitioner content in this focus area is measurably stale and in one case wrong. Search surfaced posts asserting a PreToolUse field named `modifyInput` (the reference documents `updatedInput`), a fixed count of 12 or 30 hook events (the reference's event table is larger and still growing), and a Sonnet 4.6 second-stage classifier (superseded by the Sonnet 5 default at v2.1.210). None of these were used to support a claim.

[claude-context-memory] Current Claude Code release is v2.1.214 (2026-07-18). Four releases landed after the 2026-07-12 baseline: 2.1.208 and 2.1.210 (both 2026-07-14), 2.1.212 (2026-07-17), 2.1.214 (2026-07-18).

[claude-context-memory] NEW in v2.1.214 (2026-07-18): an ISO `modified` timestamp is now added to memory file frontmatter. Directly relevant to this bucket — memory files now carry machine-readable recency, which makes freshness/staleness policies over auto memory implementable for the first time.

[claude-context-memory] NEW in v2.1.212 (2026-07-17): token usage reduced in inter-agent messaging — `SendMessage` bodies are no longer duplicated into replayed history and tool results. Changes the context cost model for multi-agent setups; any prior measurement of inter-agent token overhead taken before 2026-07-17 is now stale.

[claude-context-memory] NEW in v2.1.210 (2026-07-14): fixed `/context` reporting 0 tokens for all tool groups on Bedrock. Any Bedrock-based context accounting collected before this date is unreliable.

[claude-context-memory] NEW in v2.1.208 (2026-07-14): several long-session memory leaks fixed (MCP stdio server stderr accumulating up to 64 MB per server; LSP documents now LRU-capped at 50 docs; async hook output retained after backgrounding; unbounded growth in headless/SDK sessions from large tool-result payloads). Also: file edit read cache now bounded to 16 MB instead of pinning up to 1,000 full files, and session transcript size reduced up to 79x in edit-heavy sessions. These are process-memory changes, not context-window changes — worth recording precisely because 'memory' in these entries does NOT mean MEMORY.md, and the two are easy to conflate in this bucket.

[claude-context-memory] NEW in v2.1.208: markdown tables over 200 rows now render only the first 200 with a '… N more rows' notice — a new truncation boundary that can silently drop tool output rows from what a reviewer sees.

[claude-context-memory] Documented behavior predating the baseline but not previously captured in this bucket: v2.1.198 made compaction summarization inherit the session's extended thinking configuration; v2.1.206 added a `/doctor` trim proposal for checked-in CLAUDE.md; v2.1.207 fixed invalid glob bracket patterns in `paths:` frontmatter breaking the Read tool for every evaluated file; v2.1.211 changed path-scoped and nested rules to respect `project` exclusion in `--setting-sources` (before v2.1.211 they loaded even when project was excluded).

[claude-context-memory] URL drift: www.anthropic.com/news/context-management now issues a 308 permanent redirect to claude.com/blog/context-management. Anthropic content is migrating off anthropic.com onto claude.com; any registered anthropic.com/news or anthropic.com/engineering URLs should be re-resolved, including the assigned source anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents.

[claude-context-memory] Default-behavior drift worth flagging for guidance rewrites: MCP tool schemas are now deferred by default with only tool names in context. Older repo guidance about pruning MCP servers primarily to save context is weakened by this default.

[claude-agents-skills] NEW since 2026-07-12 baseline: v2.1.212 (2026-07-17) added a per-session subagent spawn cap, default 200, override CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION, reset by /clear. First hard first-party ceiling on delegation fan-out.

[claude-agents-skills] NEW since baseline: v2.1.215 stopped Claude from auto-invoking the /verify and /code-review skills; they now require explicit /verify or /code-review. Breaks any workflow assuming spontaneous verification.

[claude-agents-skills] NEW since baseline: v2.1.211 — subagents (and context compaction) now inherit the session's extended thinking configuration; background subagent results now reach Claude only via a completion notification, so Claude no longer reports results for a subagent that has not finished; /usage session totals now reset on /clear instead of accumulating for the process lifetime.

[claude-agents-skills] NEW since baseline: v2.1.210 security fix — isolation: 'worktree' subagents could previously run git-mutating commands against the main repo checkout. Any repo guidance recommending worktree isolation as a containment boundary must require v2.1.210+.

[claude-agents-skills] Recent but pre-baseline, newly recorded this pass: v2.1.207 changed agent-team mailbox handling so malformed entries are reported and removed while valid messages still deliver; before v2.1.207 a single malformed entry caused a repeated per-second error and blocked that mailbox until manually deleted.

[claude-agents-skills] Recent but pre-baseline: v2.1.199 changed idle-teammate row behavior in the agent panel (idle rows now hide only once every agent is idle, and /model or /fast typed while viewing a teammate now shows a notice that the change applies to the lead), and stacked slash-skill invocations now load up to 5 leading skills instead of only the first.

[claude-agents-skills] Default flip to watch: teammateMode default changed from "auto" to "in-process" at v2.1.179, so sessions upgraded from earlier versions that previously opened split panes now stay in one terminal unless the mode is set explicitly.

[claude-agents-skills] API removal to watch: v2.1.178 removed the TeamCreate and TeamDelete tools; every session now has one implicit team when CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1. The team_name input on the Agent tool and the team_name field in TaskCreated / TaskCompleted / TeammateIdle hook payloads are accepted but deprecated and now carry a session-derived name.

[claude-agents-skills] Default flip already in force: v2.1.198 made subagents run in the background by default; previously Claude chose per task. Also at v2.1.198 the built-in Explore agent began inheriting the main session's model (capped at opus) instead of running on haiku, which raises Explore's cost profile.

[claude-agents-skills] Registered source staleness: the tembo.io orchestration post still cites 'Claude Code v2.1.32 or later' as the agent-teams minimum and documents 'Shift+Down' for teammate navigation; current tier-1 docs describe post-v2.1.178 setup-free spawning and up/down arrow keys. Recommended for retirement.

[codex-config-hooks] DOCS HOST MIGRATION: developers.openai.com/codex/* now 308-redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*. Two of the five assigned sources were affected. Old links still resolve, so this is silent drift that would not show up as a fetch failure.

[codex-config-hooks] PATH CHANGE, not just a host swap: config-advanced moved from /codex/config-advanced to /docs/config-file/config-advanced, gaining a /config-file/ segment. The hooks page did NOT gain an equivalent segment (/docs/hooks), so the two pages migrated under different path conventions -- do not pattern-rewrite registry URLs mechanically.

[codex-config-hooks] REGISTRY DUPLICATION EXPOSED: after redirect resolution, assigned sources #1 (developers.openai.com/codex/hooks) and #4 (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) are the same page. The bucket has been spending two fetches per cycle on one document.

[codex-config-hooks] RELEASE CADENCE IN WINDOW: five stable patch releases shipped between the 2026-07-12 baseline and today -- 0.144.2 and 0.144.3 (2026-07-13), 0.144.4 (2026-07-14), 0.144.5 (2026-07-16), 0.144.6 (2026-07-18). Baseline version anchor should move to 0.144.6.

[codex-config-hooks] NEXT MINOR IN PRERELEASE: the 0.145.0 alpha line is active and iterating fast (0.145.0-alpha.20 through alpha.24 all within 2026-07-17/18). Config and hook surfaces in this bucket should be re-verified when 0.145.0 reaches stable.

[codex-config-hooks] NO SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE TO THE BUCKET'S SUBJECT MATTER: no changelog entry dated on or after 2026-07-12 touches hooks, config.toml, AGENTS.md, project_doc, trust, or requirements.toml. The hook event vocabulary, handler types, trust model, and AGENTS.md hierarchy all appear stable across this window. The releases in the window were bug fixes (context-window corrections, dangerous-command detection, TUI rendering).

[codex-config-hooks] PRIOR-WINDOW HOOK ACTIVITY (context, pre-baseline): 0.143.0 (2026-07-08) relaxed hooks.json top-level metadata validation and 0.144.0 (2026-07-09) emitted canonical hook prompt items. Both predate the 2026-07-12 baseline but indicate the hooks subsystem was being actively changed immediately before this window.

[codex-exec-automation] VERSION DRIFT: Codex CLI stable advanced from the 0.144.2/0.144.3 line (on/around the 2026-07-12 baseline) to 0.144.6, released 2026-07-18. A 0.145.0-alpha line is active, reaching 0.145.0-alpha.24 on 2026-07-18.

[codex-exec-automation] 0.144.6 (2026-07-18) refreshed bundled instructions for GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna and CORRECTED their context windows to 272,000 tokens. Any context-budget arithmetic pinned before this release used a wrong window value.

[codex-exec-automation] 0.144.5 (2026-07-16) expanded dangerous-command detection to more forced `rm` forms and added clearer rejection reasons. This is a behaviour-narrowing change: unattended automation that previously executed forced deletes may now be denied.
[codex-exec-automation] 0.144.4 (2026-07-14) and 0.144.3 (2026-07-13) are maintenance/version-only releases with no user-facing changes.

[codex-exec-automation] 0.144.2 (2026-07-13) ROLLED BACK a prompting regression, restoring the previous Guardian auto-review policy, request format and tool behaviour. Any observation of Guardian behaviour recorded between 0.144.0 and 0.144.2 may reflect the regressed prompt, not intended behaviour.

[codex-exec-automation] HOST MIGRATION: developers.openai.com/codex/* now issues 308 Permanent Redirects to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*. Confirmed for /codex/cli/features -> /docs/codex/cli, /codex/cli/reference -> /docs/developer-commands?surface=cli, and /codex/config -> /docs/config. Every registered developers.openai.com/codex URL in this bucket needs its URL rewritten. Note the blog path (developers.openai.com/blog/...) did NOT redirect and still resolves directly.

[codex-exec-automation] FEATURE DEPRECATION: Codex custom prompts (~/.codex/prompts/, /prompts:<name>) are now explicitly deprecated in favour of skills. This changes the recommended answer to 'how do I package a reusable command' from custom prompts to .agents/skills/SKILL.md, and makes skills the surface that supports implicit invocation.

[codex-exec-automation] REGISTRY SCOPE ERROR (not a vendor change): the registered 'developer-commands' source does not document user-authored custom commands at all - it is a built-in slash-command and CLI-subcommand reference. If the bucket's 'developer/custom commands' focus was resting on this URL, that focus was pointed at the wrong page; build-skills is the correct target.

[codex-exec-automation] BROKEN DOCS LINK: learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config returns HTTP 404 while developers.openai.com/codex/config 308-redirects to it - a redirect into a dead page. The authoritative approval/sandbox config reference is currently unreachable by URL, likely collateral from the host migration.

[codex-exec-automation] TIER-5 ACCURACY FLAG: the registered danielvaughan archiving post asserts archived sessions are moved to ~/.codex/archived_sessions/ and that session files are world-readable (mode 0644). The first conflicts with the tier-1 PR (archive is an RPC-driven metadata flag) and with the post's own later text; the second is uncorroborated. Neither was promoted to a claim.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] DOC DOMAIN MIGRATION: all developers.openai.com/codex/* URLs now HTTP 308 to learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*, and the path structure changed too (/codex/subagents → /docs/agent-configuration/subagents; /codex/changelog → /docs/changelog; /codex/config-reference → /docs/config-file/config-reference). Every registered OpenAI Codex doc URL in the manifest needs rewriting, not just a host swap.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] SANDBOX BACKEND: the current codex-rs/linux-sandbox README describes bubblewrap (bwrap) as the primary Linux backend with Landlock demoted to a legacy opt-in behind features.use_legacy_landlock. Widely circulated third-party writeups (and search-result summaries) still describe Codex on Linux as 'Landlock plus seccomp'. Any repo guidance carrying the Landlock framing is stale.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] RELEASES IN WINDOW (since 2026-07-12): 0.144.3 (2026-07-13), 0.144.5 (2026-07-16, expanded dangerous-command detection with clearer rejection feedback), 0.144.6 (2026-07-18, stable). Pre-releases 0.145.0-alpha.22/.23/.24 landed 2026-07-17/18, indicating a 0.145.0 line is in flight.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] CONTEXT WINDOW CHANGE: 0.144.6 corrected GPT-5.6 Sol / Terra / Luna context windows to 272,000 tokens. A user issue (#32806, filed 2026-07-13 against 0.144.3, now closed) reported this as a drop from a previously observed 372K raw. Any cost/budget figures in the repo keyed to a larger GPT-5.6 window are now wrong.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] NEW SUBAGENT DEFECT REPORTS IN WINDOW: #33039 (2026-07-14) and #33447 (2026-07-15), both open and both alleging Codex Desktop caps concurrent agent threads at 4 regardless of agents.max_threads. Neither has maintainer confirmation. This is the first sign that the documented concurrency knob may not be authoritative on every surface.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] SUBAGENT ERROR PROPAGATION: recent release notes indicate parent agents now receive terminal subagent errors instead of seeing failed work as an empty successful completion, and subagent MCP startup warnings now stay in the owning thread. Relevant to this repo's silent_defect_rate work — a previously silent failure mode in Codex orchestration appears to have been closed. Exact version not pinned; verify before relying on it.

[codex-subagents-sandbox] MCP AUTH: changelog entry for 0.144.0 (2026-07-09, just before the baseline) states MCP tools can now request authentication interactively without an experimental opt-in. Just outside the window but likely not yet reflected in repo guidance.

[security-sandboxing-injection] Claude Code sandbox settings surface moved substantially within the v2.1.x line, and the official docs carry explicit min-version markers that make the drift auditable: `sandbox.credentials` requires v2.1.187+; per-session host allow-on-approval (choosing Yes allows the host for the rest of the session rather than re-prompting) landed in v2.1.191; `"mode": "mask"` credential substitution and the experimental `network.tlsTerminate` setting require v2.1.199+; symlink resolution for protected settings-file deny rules landed in v2.1.210; plan-mode behaviour changed in v2.1.212.

[security-sandboxing-injection] Behavioural change to flag for any repo guidance written before v2.1.212: a bare `Bash` ask rule (or the `Bash(*)` form) is skipped for commands that run sandboxed, BUT as of v2.1.212 the rule is no longer skipped in plan mode — it now prompts for sandboxed commands including read-only ones. Correspondingly, auto-allow in plan mode now runs only read-only commands without a prompt. Before v2.1.212 both skips applied in plan mode too, so guidance authored against the older behaviour now over-promises silence.

[security-sandboxing-injection] `network.tlsTerminate` is new and still labelled experimental. It is the first Anthropic-shipped answer to the domain-fronting weakness in the default hostname-only allowlist, but the docs are explicit that it exists to enable credential masking and does NOT add content filtering — so it does not close the exfiltration gap on its own.

[security-sandboxing-injection] OWASP's flagship agentic document changed edition and character since the 2025 baseline: 'State of Agentic AI Security and Governance' went v1.0 (July 2025) to v2.01 (June 2026), replacing a catalog of plausible threats with disclosed CVEs, vendor advisories and breach reports, and adding a live incidents/exploits tracker, revised agent taxonomy, enterprise adoption maturity model, and new sections on agent identity, AI SBOM, supply-chain provenance and regulatory landscape.

[security-sandboxing-injection] New primary literature appeared inside the 2026-07-12 baseline window worth tracking: arXiv:2606.26479 (submitted 2026-06-25) is the first adaptive evaluation aimed specifically at out-of-band prompt-injection defenses (CaMeL, FIDES, Progent, RTBAS, FORGE), and reports a preliminary result that runs opposite to the in-band detection collapse documented in arXiv:2510.09023. Direction of the field is shifting from 'can we detect injections' to 'can deterministic enforcement survive adaptive attack'.

[security-sandboxing-injection] Framework-level CVEs now exist for the prompt-injection-to-RCE path: CVE-2026-26030 (semantic-kernel Python <1.39.4) and CVE-2026-25592 (Semantic Kernel .NET SDK <1.71.0), disclosed 2026-05-07. Any pinned Semantic Kernel dependency in the estate should be checked against these floors.

[security-sandboxing-injection] Two registered sandbox-comparison sources are being retiered t3 to t5 this pass after inspection revealed they are vendor self-comparisons rather than neutral engineering reports. This is a registry-quality drift, not an upstream content change, but it changes what those entries may be cited for.

[evals-judging] In-window change (post 2026-07-12): arXiv:2607.01211 'Are Performance-Optimization Benchmarks Reliably Measuring Coding Agents?' posted v2 on 2026-07-16 (v1 was 2026-07-01). Claims evals-judging-21 through -23 are drawn from the current version; if a 2026-07-12 baseline captured v1, the replay-validity and score-weight figures should be re-read against v2.

[evals-judging] In-window change (post 2026-07-12): the BenchLM benchmark registry was last updated 2026-07-14 and now tracks 296 benchmark definitions across 10 categories. Tier 5, no primary citations, recorded as an index only.

[evals-judging] Boundary item: arXiv:2607.10080 (multilingual injection against LLM relevance judges) was submitted 2026-07-11, one day before the window. Flagged as new material relative to a 2026-07-12 baseline pass that would likely have missed it.

[evals-judging] Recent but pre-window, and new relative to this bucket's prior coverage: arXiv:2607.05904 (2026-07-07, self-play judge reward hacking) and arXiv:2607.07189 (2026-07-08, ImagingBench). Neither appears to have been previously registered.

[evals-judging] Substantive contradiction against practitioner guidance: the assigned tier-5 source treats verbosity bias as a first-order judge failure requiring length penalties or token normalization, but tier-2 measurement (arXiv:2606.19544, 2026-06-17) finds the effect below 0.011 under a single pairwise rubric. Position bias, by contrast, is confirmed as severe (>0.10) even in judges with >0.95 test-retest reliability. Any repo guidance that ranks verbosity bias above position bias should be revised.

[evals-judging] Assigned source content drift: futureagi.com/blog/llm-as-a-judge was originally published 2025-01-29 and updated 2026-05-14. Its substance is now partly superseded by tier-2 measurement; its registered tier of 5 remains correct.

[evals-judging] Emerging consensus shift worth tracking: three independent 2026 sources (arXiv:2607.05904, arXiv:2607.01211, sourcegraph/CodeScaleBench) converge on preferring held-out or execution-derived oracles over LLM-judge scoring wherever a deterministic check exists. The CodeScaleBench harness scores with patch-based and artifact verifiers and no LLM judge at all.

[drift-discovery] SUMMARISATION HAZARD OBSERVED THIS PASS: a first-pass summary of the Claude Code changelog mis-attributed roughly a dozen 2.1.214 bullets to 2.1.215. A verbatim re-fetch showed 2.1.215 contains exactly ONE bullet. All version attributions in this report were re-derived from verbatim quotes.
